properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. musicjug's idea §6 and complaint §7, 2026-08-31.

The session made roughly ten separate tool-schema lookups across one session, each a round trip, because it could not know it would need `delete_edge` until a cycle appeared or `set_interface_designation` until a gap asked for it. "A reflow2 session therefore has a high call-count floor."

⭐ THE PART THAT MATTERS IS NOT THE COST, IT IS THE MISS: "This is the deferred-tool harness rather than reflow2 proper. But reflow2 ships `find_tools`, and I never used it because nothing told me how it differs from the harness's own search — so the one mitigation that exists was invisible from where I sat."

TWO IDEAS, AS ORIGINALLY RECORDED:
· **SAY WHAT `find_tools` IS FOR.** It exists, it is served, and an agent with a tool-discovery problem did not reach for it because it could not tell it apart from the host's search. That is a positioning fix, not a code one.
· **BUNDLES.** `find_tools("genesis")`, or a `bundle` argument, returning the ~12 schemas that workflow needs in one call, so an agent loads once rather than ten times.

⚠️ THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT ON BUNDLES: loading twelve schemas an agent may not need is not obviously cheaper than loading four it does, and a bundle that guesses wrong costs both. The measured problem is that the lookups are UNPREDICTABLE — needed only when a gap or a defect appears — which is exactly the case a fixed bundle cannot anticipate. A bundle keyed to a SKILL rather than to a workflow phase might fare better, since the skill knows what it is about to ask for, but nobody has checked which tools each skill actually uses.

📌 THIS IS A KNOWN SHAPE HERE, and worth connecting: reflow2 has a recorded doctrine that a capability reaches a user only with a typed tool, an instruction, AND a detector that notices absence. `find_tools` has the tool and no instruction pointing at it — which is the same leg missing as in several of the day's other findings, and the cheapest one to fix anywhere.

⚠️ SEPARATELY AND NOT THE SAME QUESTION: the report's §1 complaint that `reflow2_start_design` requires a client restart before any design tool exists — "the FIRST thing a new user experiences, and a hard stop requiring manual action mid-flow." That belongs to the existing stranded-server family (`fact:defect-rebuild-strands-the-shared-server`, `fact:defect-the-latent-surface-never-re-probes-after-a-cli-restore`) rather than here, but it is the same session's first impression and nobody has asked whether the first-run case differs from the rebuild case.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐ PRIOR ART, ADDED 2026-09-01 ON ANTHONY'S POINTER — AND IT ARGUES AGAINST BUNDLES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The **Agentic Resource Discovery specification** (ARD, `github.com/ards-project/ard-spec`, v0.91, ~443 stars; local clone `/home/ajs7/project/ard-spec`) is a published standard for exactly this problem, argued through in the open. Its own framing is the same sentence as musicjug's complaint: *"The bottleneck is no longer invocation. It is discovery."*

THREE OF ITS NINE ADRs TRANSFER DIRECTLY, and they were reasoned rather than invented:

**① ADR-0001 — THE ANSWER TO THE BUNDLES PROBLEM WAS NOT BUNDLES.** ARD hit the same need (a client cannot plan without knowing what a collection holds) and answered it with `POST /explore`: dynamic FACET AGGREGATION over the collection, where an empty query returns whole-collection statistics and a real query returns counts over that subset. Its stated reason for preferring this over pre-computed statistics is that it is "mathematically a superset" — one endpoint serves both cheap global shape and query-scoped planning.

⭐ THAT IS A BETTER ANSWER THAN A BUNDLE TO THE PROBLEM MUSICJUG ACTUALLY HAD, and it is the objection already recorded above arrived at from a different direction. A bundle guesses what an agent will need; a facet answer lets the agent see the shape of the 165 tools and decide for itself. It also cannot go stale the way a hand-maintained bundle list would — and it answers the "bundle keyed to a skill" variant too, since a skill could ask for the facets it cares about rather than having a list maintained for it.

**② ADR-0004 — SEPARATE RELEVANCE SEARCH FROM DETERMINISTIC BROWSE, and do not let either grow into the other.** ARD refused complex boolean filter strings and custom sort orders inside `POST /search`, splitting them to `GET /agents`. Two of its three reasons are already measured facts here: sorting by metadata "conflicts with and destroys relevance-based ranking"; and asking an LLM to emit complex filter strings is "error-prone and prone to LLM parser hallucinations" — the same class as reflow2's own prose-field parameter-swallowing defect fixed in #404. `find_tools` today is one call doing both jobs.

**③ ADR-0005 — WRAP THE FILTER OBJECT so caller-supplied keys cannot collide with reserved protocol keywords**, and share one query envelope across endpoints so a client learns the shape once. Directly relevant to any `bundle` or filter argument added to `find_tools`.

📌 WHAT TO DO WITH THIS IS STILL OPEN, and the prior art narrows the question rather than settling it: is the ask a **positioning fix**, an **`/explore`-shaped facet answer** over reflow2's own tool surface, or **both**? The positioning half remains the cheapest thing on this list and is independent of the rest.

⚠️ AND A SEPARATE, LARGER QUESTION THIS RAISES BUT DOES NOT ASK: reflow2 is itself an undiscoverable agentic resource — every user so far arrived because Anthony handed it to them, and usage rather than features is the recorded bottleneck. Whether reflow2 should PUBLISH an ARD entry is a positioning decision with real trade-offs (a pre-1.0 tool with an unsettled licence, exposed via a pre-1.0 standard) and it is Anthony's to make, not this node's.

📌 THE SPEC IS NOT REGISTERED AS AN ARTIFACT. It lives outside this repo and is not ours to copy in; `dec:idea-how-is-a-source-outside-the-repo-registered` is the open question about how to record such a source, so the URL and local path above stand in for a registration until that is settled.

🛑 A NOTE ON HOW THIS NODE WAS EDITED, because it is evidence for a defect this design is tracking: sharpening it dropped the two paragraphs above (the three-legs connection, and the bootstrap question) and the revision warning caught it — the prior value existed only in that tool reply. That is `fact:the-revision-warning-holds-the-only-copy-of-what-it-warns-was-lost` happening to the session recording it, and it is the argument for `snapshot_prior` in one line.
properties.name: OPEN — reflow2 ships `find_tools` and an agent never used it because nothing said how it differs from the harness's own search. Fix the pitch, serve bundles, or take ARD's answer?

properties.rationale:
musicjug's ideas, relayed. The three-legs connection and the bootstrap-family pointer are this project's own context and were not available to the reporter.

PRIOR ART ADDED 2026-09-01 at Anthony's pointer. It is recorded here rather than as a second idea because it answers the SAME open question — a node holding one question with new evidence, not two questions.

⚠️ THE HONEST LIMIT ON BORROWING FROM ARD: it is four months old and at v0.91, so adopting its shapes couples a pre-1.0 tool to a pre-1.0 standard. READING its ADRs carries none of that risk and is what is proposed here; implementing an ARD-shaped interface, or publishing into ARD, is a different decision with a different cost and has not been taken.

📌 AND THE COMPARISON IS NOT EXACT. ARD's endpoints search a collection of THIRD-PARTY resources whose descriptions the service does not control; `find_tools` searches 165 tools reflow2 itself authors and can describe however it likes. That asymmetry may make the facet answer cheaper here than it was for them, or may make it unnecessary — nobody has checked which.
